title: RansomwareHelp co-founder Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar indicted on wire fraud counts over ransomware recovery service
date_note: BankInfoSecurity (26 November) says the DOJ announced the charges on Wednesday (25 November) and that the indictment was returned on 18 November; 404 Media first reported it the week before.
summary: BankInfoSecurity reports a Rhode Island grand jury returned an indictment on 18 November charging Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, co-founder and CTO of Florida-based RansomwareHelp, with three counts of wire fraud. Court documents say the firm told victims it could recover their network without paying the ransom or negotiating with the threat actor. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department said Palacio charged the undercover victim company more than double what he paid the undercover ransomware actor.
plain: A man who ran a ransomware data-recovery firm has been charged with wire fraud. Court documents say the firm told victims it could recover their network without paying the ransom or negotiating with the threat actor.
exec: Per court documents cited by BankInfoSecurity, a firm sold ransomware recovery to victims while the charges allege it dealt with the ransomware actor; check any recovery vendor's claims.
geo_basis: The indictment was returned by a Rhode Island federal grand jury, per the article; city assumed as the federal court seat.

sources.name: BankInfoSecurity: FBI Busts 'Wolf in Sheep's Clothing' Ransomware Responder

validation.note: Single source: BankInfoSecurity (govinfosecurity.com is the same publisher). 404 Media's article was only partly readable (paywall); the DOJ release was not found.
